Compared with the prior single-sentence focus, the full FOMC statement projects a balanced, risk‑managed stance: economic activity is expanding at a solid pace and unemployment is low (positive), but inflation remains somewhat elevated and uncertainty has increased, with the Committee explicitly noting higher risks of both unemployment and inflation (tempering). Holding the federal funds rate at 4.25–4.50% while continuing balance‑sheet reduction—slowing Treasury runoff to a $5B cap and allowing up to $35B/month MBS runoff with reinvestment into Treasuries—signals a cautious, data‑dependent posture. This is broadly consistent with Taylor‑rule prescriptions when inflation is above the 2% PCE target and the labor market is tight (Taylor, 1993; FOMC uses PCE), and with forward‑looking New Keynesian guidance emphasizing data dependence and expectations management (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). The heightened uncertainty language aligns with risk‑management under model uncertainty (Wieland, 2000a,b) and targeting‑rule analyses that weigh inflation/output-gap tradeoffs (Svensson and Woodford, 2003; 2004). Net tone: slightly positive on current activity/labor, tempered by inflation and uncertainty, hence modestly positive overall.
